title: [WT-14] Wrappers: worktree removal at DONE and the orphan sweep
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §1.7, §1.9 and §1.10.

Objective: worktrees do not pile up. Removal never deletes an unlanded commit without a rescue ref, and never recurses through a junction into the control checkout's .serena/memories or .claude/skills.

Deliverable, in scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 as twins:
- QA post-flight: after qa_approve leaves the task DONE, and only if task_branch_landed / Test-MoeTaskBranchLanded (from WT-04) is true, remove W and `git branch -D moe/task/<taskId>`.
- Orphan sweep at any wrapper's loop top:
  - at most once per MOE_WORKTREE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SEC (default 3600), under the mkdir lock <gitdir>/moe/worktree/sweep.lock (older than 2 h counts as stale and is broken; a held lock skips the pass), at most 5 worktrees per pass;
  - candidates: registered worktrees under .worktrees/ whose task is DONE, ARCHIVED or unknown, with no open attempt;
  - per candidate: commit dirty non-DENY bytes to a rescue ref (reason worktree-orphan); rescue the branch tip if it is not fully landed; then unlink, unlock, `git worktree remove --force --force`, and `git branch -D`.
- Unlinking: every path in <gitdir>/moe/worktree/<taskId>.links is unlinked first (sh `rm -- <link>`, ps1 `cmd /c rmdir <link>`) and verified gone; then the manifest and the .control-dirt file are deleted. Any unlink or remove failure gives MOE_WORKTREE_REMOVE_REFUSED: W stays, and the next pass retries.
- A directory under .worktrees/ that git does not list is never deleted: MOE_WORKTREE_UNREGISTERED, one #general alert per path per day.
- Cases in scripts/tests/postflight.sh and postflight.ps1. Depends on WT-13 (task-fbe8e3880ddf47dfa8546f220acea770).

NOT in scope: pruning grok trusted_folders entries; removing worktrees of non-terminal tasks; docs (WT-18).

Verification: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh (and on a Windows seat: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell)
definitionOfDone: postflight case (both harnesses): a QA approval of a fully landed task removes .worktrees/<taskId> and deletes moe/task/<taskId>; the control checkout's .serena/memories and .claude/skills still exist with their contents.

postflight case: the sweep removes a DONE task's worktree whose branch has an unlanded commit only after creating refs/moe/rescue/<taskId>/<ts> (reason worktree-orphan) at that commit; dirty W bytes are on a rescue ref too.
postflight case: a worktree whose task has an open attempt or is WORKING is never touched; a held sweep.lock skips the pass; at most 5 removals per pass.
postflight case: an unregistered directory under .worktrees/ prints MOE_WORKTREE_UNREGISTERED and is left on disk; a forced unlink failure prints MOE_WORKTREE_REMOVE_REFUSED and leaves W registered.
Existing postflight and worktree-landing cases pass unchanged; both wrappers carry the same MOE_WORKTREE_/MOE_LAND_/MOE_CONTROL_/MOE_BOARD_ codes; the verification command exits 0.

implementationPlan.description:
sh: the junction-safe removal engine and the QA DONE removal, with their postflight.sh cases (DoD 1, DoD 4 unlink half, comment-dc04a1d3).

First read the landed bytes this builds on, and reuse them; never re-implement a landed helper:
- WT-04: task_branch_landed REF TASKID, the `worktree list --porcelain -z` parser, and the D:\ vs /mnt/d path normalization.
- WT-06: the link manifest writer, its line format and its location under the common git dir.
- WT-07: the control-seat predicate control_worktree_mode, the worktree attribution with denied_wt, the local MOE_TOP/MOE_REL/MOE_GITDIR shadow, and the .control-dirt path.
- WT-13: the target rule (consolidationBranch or main) and the #general alert throttle.
Where a landed name differs from this plan, use the landed one and list the mapping in complete_task's summary. sh editing rule: write the whole file elsewhere on the same filesystem, run `bash -n`, then one `mv -f`. New helpers go above the main-loop `{ ... exit }` group. Every new line must be set -e safe.

New helpers (D = `<common git dir>/moe/worktree`, from `git -C <top> rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`):
- worktree_lock_take / worktree_lock_drop:
  - take = `mkdir -p D`, then `mkdir D/sweep.lock`.
  - A held lock whose mtime is older than 7200s is stale: `rmdir` it once and retry mkdir once.
  - Never sleep or wait. A held lock returns 1.
  - drop rmdirs the lock only if this process took it.
- remove_task_worktree TOP TID, the one engine both callers use. Each guard failure prints `[WARN] MOE_WORKTREE_REMOVE_REFUSED: <W>: <detail>` and returns 1, leaving W registered and the branch kept:
  1. TID must match `^task-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$`, and W = TOP/.worktrees/TID.
  2. Refuse when W or TOP/.worktrees is itself a link.
  3. The porcelain must list W on refs/heads/moe/task/TID. A W recorded in the other OS's spelling gets `git worktree repair` first, as WT-04 does.
  4. Refuse when W/.moe exists (`[ -e ] || [ -L ]`).
  5. Manifest D/TID.links: each non-empty line is a W-relative path.
     - Refuse a line that is absolute, has a drive letter or backslash, or has an empty, '.' or '..' segment.
     - Refuse when any ancestor of the entry inside W is a link, so nothing is ever reached through a parent link.
     - An entry that is a link: `rm -- "$W/$rel"`, then verify it is gone (`[ -e ] || [ -L ]` both false).
     - A missing entry is an unused reservation: skip it.
     - An entry that exists but is not a link is W's own bytes: leave it for the remove.
  6. `git -C TOP worktree remove --force --force W`. There is no separate unlock: a double force removes a locked worktree, and a failed remove keeps W's lock against a cross-OS prune. This deliberately differs from §1.9's unlock-then-remove. Put git's first stderr line in the detail.
  7. Delete exactly D/TID.links and D/TID.control-dirt. A missing file is fine; a failed delete is a [WARN]. Never glob-delete under D: journals live there.
  8. `git -C TOP branch -D moe/task/TID`. A failure is a [WARN]; W is already gone.
  9. Print `[worktree] removed <W> on moe/task/TID`.
- qa_done_worktree_removal TID. Return 0 silently unless all of these hold: the control predicate is true, git_top resolves with MOE_REL empty, and W is registered. Then:
  - Leave W with `[worktree] left <W> to the orphan sweep: <reason>` when:
    - W/.moe exists;
    - the porcelain branch is not moe/task/TID;
    - W holds non-DENY dirt, or the status check fails (WT-07 attribution, the list a checkpoint would land);
    - task_branch_landed refs/heads/<target> TID fails;
    - the lock is held.
  - Otherwise: engine, then drop the lock.
  - This path never rescues and never deletes anything else.
- Call site: the task-holding post-flight branch, after finalize_postflight and live_marker_remove: `if [ "$ROLE" = qa ] && [ "$FINAL_STATUS" = DONE ]; then qa_done_worktree_removal "$PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID" || true; fi`. It must never change LAND_OUTCOME, POSTFLIGHT_BREAK, finalize or the exit code.

Tests in postflight.sh. Write ONE fixture builder:
- control on moe/control;
- W made exactly as WT-04 makes it (`worktree add --lock --no-checkout -b`, then sparse `'/*' '!/.moe/'`, then `read-tree -mu HEAD`);
- control .serena/memories/sentinel.md and .claude/skills/s/SKILL.md;
- W/.serena/memories and W/.claude/skills linked to them with WT-06's harness helper, or else `ln -s` (a node junction on msys);
- the manifest written in WT-06's format.
Test teardown unlinks its own links before deleting scratch. Cases are table-driven, with `[scenario WT14A]` style names; bump the harness scenario counters per the landed convention.
- WT14A (DoD 1): a landed branch (target holds the task commit's tree), ROLE qa, FAKE_TASK_STATUS=DONE. W is absent from disk and from the porcelain; moe/task/TID, .links and .control-dirt are gone; both control sentinels are byte-identical.
- WT14B: as A, plus W/.moe/x. W, the branch, the manifest and .moe/x are kept, and the sentinels are intact.
- WT14C: as A, plus a modified tracked file in W. W is kept, with the `left ... orphan sweep` line.
- WT14D (DoD 4): as A, with `chmod 0555` on W/.serena so the unlink fails. Expect MOE_WORKTREE_REMOVE_REFUSED; W stays registered; the branch, the link and the sentinels are intact. Restore the mode in teardown. When `id -u` is 0, print `[scenario WT14D] SKIP (root ignores mode bits)`.
- WT14S (rail 4): control on a shared moe/work-* branch with a registered DONE W. Nothing is removed, and no MOE_WORKTREE_ or [worktree] line appears.
Error handling: every git call's failure maps to REFUSED or to the leave-to-sweep path, never to a deletion.

sh: the orphan sweep at the loop top, the fake-proxy status knob, and the postflight.sh cases (DoD 2, DoD 3, DoD 4 unregistered half).

worktree_orphan_sweep. Run order:
1. Gate, silent: return 0 unless the control predicate is true, git_top resolves with MOE_REL empty, and TOP/.worktrees exists.
2. Interval: MOE_WORKTREE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SEC.
   - Unset or blank means 3600.
   - `^[0-9]{1,9}$` is used as given; 0 means every loop top, which the tests need.
   - Anything else prints one [WARN] and uses 3600.
   - Stamp file D/sweep.last holds epoch seconds. Pre-check it without the lock and return when `now-last < interval` (a stamp in the future counts as stale).
3. worktree_lock_take. A held lock prints `[worktree] sweep skipped: lock held` and returns 0.
4. Under the lock:
   - re-check the stamp;
   - write now with a temp file plus mv (a failed write is a [WARN] and skips the pass);
   - run worktree_sweep_pass;
   - always drop the lock.

worktree_sweep_pass:
- Enumerate with `git -C TOP worktree list --porcelain -z`, through WT-04's parser and normalization. A failure aborts the pass with a [WARN].
- Registered set: entries whose normalized path's parent is exactly TOP/.worktrees.
- Candidates are the subset whose basename matches the TID pattern. Others, such as the main worktree and the temp hook and gate worktrees, are ignored.
- Unregistered: each DIRECTORY directly under TOP/.worktrees whose normalized path is not in the registered set.
  - Print `[WARN] MOE_WORKTREE_UNREGISTERED: <path>: not a registered worktree; left on disk`.
  - chat_send one #general alert per path per 24h, through WT-13's throttle helper keyed by a hash of the normalized path. If the helper is hour-only, add optional key and window arguments without changing its existing calls.
  - Never delete it.
- Per candidate, in TID sort order, local checks first:
  - Skip when W/.moe exists, with a `[worktree] sweep left <W>: W/.moe exists (MOE_WORKTREE_MOE_PRESENT)` line.
  - Skip when the branch is not moe/task/TID (REFUSED detail).
  - Skip when any control-project .moe/attempts/*.json record (read as utf-8-sig) has taskId TID and a phase other than 'closed'.
    - An unparsable attempt record aborts the pass: it cannot be proved not to be TID's.
  - Then `moe_rpc_unserved get_context {taskId, view:'status'}`. The status view writes nothing, unlike the default view's contextFetchedBy stamp.
    - A reply whose task.id equals TID gives the status. Only DONE or ARCHIVED make a candidate.
    - A failure whose stderr JSON carries data.codeName TASK_NOT_FOUND means unknown, which is a candidate. Reuse launch_outage_release's codeName parse.
    - Anything else aborts the pass: a transport failure, any other refusal, or a missing or mismatched task. An RPC failure never counts as unknown.
- Per candidate, removal phase, stopping after 5 candidates have reached it (removed or refused):
  a. Non-DENY dirt (WT-07 attribution in W, under the same local shadow WT-07 uses, plus `local FROZEN_TREE="" LAND_TASK_ID=TID LAND_TITLE='worktree orphan'`) goes through `rescue_ref worktree-orphan <cand>`.
  b. When task_branch_landed refs/heads/<target> TID fails, run `rescue_ref_from_commit <tip> worktree-orphan`.
  c. Proceed only when each needed rescue ref resolves to the commit just written. Dirt that rescue_ref reports as matching HEAD has nothing to lose. Anything else is REFUSED with 'rescue failed'.
  d. Re-read the attempt records right before the engine. A record that appeared now means skip.
  e. remove_task_worktree TOP TID.
- Call site: the loop top, after WT-13's follow and the wrapper reload check, just above `# -------- Pre-flight: perform startup rituals`: `worktree_orphan_sweep || true`. It never sleeps, never blocks on the lock and never changes claim behavior.

scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js, one knob, FAKE_TASK_STATUS_MAP: a comma list of `taskId=STATUS`.
- It applies only to get_context with view 'status', which no wrapper sent before this task. Answer it BEFORE the context-count block, so the attempt-finalizing flip never sees sweep reads.
- A mapped STATUS answers {contextScope:'status', task:{id, status}}.
- NOT_FOUND answers a refusal with data.codeName 'TASK_NOT_FOUND'.
- FAIL answers an error without a codeName.
- An unmapped id answers WORKING, which is never a candidate.
- Every other call is byte-identical.

Cases in postflight.sh, using step 1's builder, with MOE_WORKTREE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SEC=0 unless stated and FAKE_CLAIM_MODE idle:
- WT14E (DoD 2): a DONE W whose branch has an unlanded commit T, plus a modified tracked file and an untracked non-DENY file. Expect:
  - a refs/moe/rescue/TID/<ts> that resolves to T exactly;
  - the chan-general log has `MOE_RESCUE_REF task=TID ... sha=<T> reason=worktree-orphan`;
  - a second rescue ref whose tree has both dirty files' bytes (`git show`);
  - then W, the branch and the manifest are gone, and the sentinels are intact.
  An unknown task (NOT_FOUND) in the same run is removed the same way.
- WT14F (DoD 3): the map holds d1..d6 DONE, w1 WORKING, a1 DONE with an open .moe/attempts record (phase running), and m1 DONE with W/.moe. One run removes exactly d1..d5. d6, w1, a1 and m1 keep their W and branch.
  - A run with a fresh D/sweep.lock removes nothing and logs `sweep skipped`.
  - A run with that lock's mtime set 3h old breaks it and removes d6.
- WT14G (DoD 4): unregistered .worktrees/stray and .worktrees/task-ghost, each with a file. Both print MOE_WORKTREE_UNREGISTERED and stay with their bytes. Two runs give exactly one chan-general row per path.
- WT14H (error handling):
  - a FAIL mapping for a candidate aborts the pass: no ref, no removal;
  - with the interval unset and a fresh sweep.last, nothing runs;
  - an invalid interval (`abc`) warns and uses 3600.

ps1 twin of step 1 (scripts/moe-agent.ps1, scripts/tests/postflight.ps1). Same contract, guard order, codes and detail text, the same `[worktree] ...` lines, and the same MOE_WORKTREE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SEC name, so parity-check and the code diff stay equal.

Functions, placed beside the landed WT-04/WT-07 twins:
- Lock-MoeWorktreeSweep and Unlock-MoeWorktreeSweep:
  - [IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory for D;
  - New-Item -ItemType Directory for the lock, in try/catch, so an existing lock is 'held';
  - the same 7200s stale break: Remove-Item without -Recurse, then one retry.
- Remove-MoeTaskWorktree -Top -TaskId, the engine.
- Invoke-MoeQaWorktreeRemoval -TaskId.

PS rules:
- Every git call goes through Invoke-MoeGit, with -MergeStderr where the detail needs git's message.
- Compare paths with the landed comparable-path normalization, then [string]::Equals(a, b, [StringComparison]::Ordinal). Use -ceq for refs and codes, and -LiteralPath everywhere.
- PS 5.1 compatible: no `&&`, no ternary.
- Link test: `(Get-Item -LiteralPath $p -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)`, then `.Attributes -band [IO.FileAttributes]::ReparsePoint`.
- Unlink:
  - On Windows, `cmd /c rmdir` on the quoted path. It removes a junction or directory link and never its target. Check $LASTEXITCODE.
  - On a non-Windows pwsh host, Remove-Item -LiteralPath -Force WITHOUT -Recurse.
  - Then verify the path is gone.
- The W/.moe test is WT-04's exact `$null -ne (Get-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path $w '.moe') -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)`.
- The lock is always released in finally.
- Call site: after the ps1 post-flight's finalize, for qa when the final status is DONE. Wrap it in try/catch, so it can never change the landing outcome, the finalize or the loop.

Tests in postflight.ps1: WT14A, WT14B, WT14C, WT14D and WT14S, mirroring step 1 with one fixture builder.
- Links are made with New-Item -ItemType Junction, or WT-06's harness helper if one landed.
- WT14D forces the unlink failure with icacls for the current user: deny DE on the junction and DC on its parent. Remove both denies in finally, so scratch cleanup works.
- Teardown removes the junctions with `cmd /c rmdir` before deleting scratch.
- Bump the ps1 scenario counters.
Error handling: as in step 1. A thrown .NET exception inside the engine becomes REFUSED, never a partial delete.

ps1 twin of step 2 (scripts/moe-agent.ps1, scripts/tests/postflight.ps1).

Invoke-MoeWorktreeSweep, called at the loop top in the same position as sh: after WT-13's follow and the reload check, before pre-flight. It runs the same gate, interval parse, stamp, lock, enumeration, unregistered alert, candidate checks and 5-cap.
- Porcelain: read `worktree list --porcelain -z` and split on "`0", reusing WT-04's ps1 parser.
- Attempt records: Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath on the control .moe/attempts. Parse each one with ConvertFrom-Json in try/catch. An unparsable record aborts the pass.
- Daemon status: Invoke-MoeRpcUnserved get_context @{taskId; view='status'}.
  - Unknown means $script:MoeRpcFailure -eq 'daemon refusal' AND $script:MoeRpcCodeName -ceq 'TASK_NOT_FOUND'.
  - Anything else non-null without a matching task.id, or a null reply, aborts the pass.
- Rescues: Invoke-MoeRescueRef with a W -Git hashtable built as WT-07's Invoke-MoeWorktreeCheckpoint builds it.
  - Dirt: -Reason worktree-orphan with -Attr @{Candidates=<non-DENY paths from Test-MoeDenyPathWorktree>}.
  - Tip: -Sha <tip> -Reason worktree-orphan.
  - Verify each ref resolves to the commit just written before the engine runs.
- Alerts: WT-13's ps1 throttle helper keyed by a path hash, with a 24h window.
- The stamp is written with a temp file plus Move-Item -Force.
- try/finally around the lock.

Tests in postflight.ps1: WT14E, WT14F, WT14G and WT14H, mirroring step 2 with the same FAKE_TASK_STATUS_MAP knob.
- Stale-lock aging: (Get-Item -LiteralPath $lock).LastWriteTime = (Get-Date).AddHours(-3).
- Keep the cases table-driven and compact. Bump the counters.
Error handling: as in step 2. No catch block may fall through to a deletion; every catch maps to REFUSED, leave-to-sweep, or abort-pass.

Size check, then the verification, run once, fresh. Its output tail is the complete_task evidence (DoD 5, and DoD 1-4 through both harnesses).

1. Size. Run `git diff --numstat` over the five files and compute net non-board LOC. If it is over 400, file ONE EPIC ADD_RAIL size exception with moe.propose_rail, in prop-d975cf4e's format:
   - name WT-14 (task-befdddf7e1f047a0ba4f71dd900c9b8f), the five files, the measured +/- and the cap you request;
   - state that it waives size only: every DoD item, the epic rails, substantive QA and fresh verification still apply.
   Do it NOW, before the long harness runs, so the governor (standing delegation, msg-aac7c9c0) can approve it while they run.

2. Verification. From the repo root in WSL, exactly:
S=$(mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/v-befdddf7.XXXXXX) && git archive HEAD scripts | tar -x -C "$S" && for f in scripts/moe-agent.sh scripts/moe-agent.ps1 scripts/tests/postflight.sh scripts/tests/postflight.ps1 scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js; do cp "$f" "$S/$f" && cmp "$f" "$S/$f" || exit 1; done && printf 'Verification snapshot: %s\n' "$S" && cd "$S" && diff <(grep -oE 'MOE_(WORKTREE|LAND|CONTROL|BOARD)_[A-Z0-9_]*' scripts/moe-agent.sh | sort -u) <(grep -oE 'MOE_(WORKTREE|LAND|CONTROL|BOARD)_[A-Z0-9_]*' scripts/moe-agent.ps1 | sort -u) && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh && env $(env | awk -F= '/^(MOE_|CLAUDE)/{printf "-u %s ", $1}') MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && env $(env | awk -F= '/^(MOE_|CLAUDE)/{printf "-u %s ", $1}') bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && WSLENV=MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 node.exe scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell

Notes on the command:
- The snapshot keeps peers' unlanded bytes out of the run.
- MOE_* and CLAUDE* are scrubbed so this seat's identity never reaches the wrappers under test.
- The ps1 harness runs through Windows node from a /mnt/d path (Serena gotcha-qa-ps1-postflight-from-wsl). On a native Windows seat, run the same chain from Git Bash with `node` for node.exe.
- Each harness run takes tens of minutes. Run it in the foreground, or poll a background run to the end.

When a run fails:
- Fix it only inside steps 1-4's files, and never weaken an assertion.
- A failure that also reproduces on a clean HEAD snapshot is pre-existing: report it with that evidence.
- Name every SKIP (WT14D as root) in the summary.
- If any byte changes after this run, re-run the whole command and submit the last output.

comments.content:
Spike self-review correction (docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §1.1, §1.9; section numbers unchanged). Where this differs from the description or my earlier comment, this comment wins.

.worktrees/ already holds worktrees that are not Moe's. The using-git-worktrees skill prefers that folder, and .worktrees/claude-efficiency-20260926 and .worktrees/main-all-20260919 exist today.

- The sweep considers only registered worktrees at .worktrees/<taskId> that are on moe/task/<taskId>.
- MOE_WORKTREE_UNREGISTERED covers only .worktrees/task-* directories.
- Nothing else under .worktrees/ is read, alerted on, rescued or removed, in any mode (rail 4).
- Add a case: a registered .worktrees/feature-x on branch feature-x and an unregistered .worktrees/scratch both survive a sweep untouched, with no alert.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
Worktree mode only, meaning the control checkout is on moe/control. Shared mode runs neither path and prints nothing.

QA removal: after qa_approve leaves a task DONE, the QA post-flight removes .worktrees/<taskId> and deletes moe/task/<taskId>, but only when every condition holds:
- the branch is fully landed (task_branch_landed against refs/heads/<target>);
- W holds no non-DENY dirt;
- W/.moe is absent;
- the sweep lock is free.
Otherwise it leaves W to the sweep.

Orphan sweep: any wrapper's loop top runs it, at most once per MOE_WORKTREE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SEC (default 3600; 0 means every loop), under a non-blocking mkdir lock (stale after 2h), with at most 5 removals per pass.
- Candidates are registered task worktrees under .worktrees/ whose task is DONE, ARCHIVED or TASK_NOT_FOUND, with no open attempt record and no W/.moe.
- Non-DENY dirt and an unlanded branch tip each get a worktree-orphan rescue ref, verified before anything is deleted.
- Manifest links are unlinked first and verified gone, then `git worktree remove --force --force`, then the manifest and control-dirt are deleted, then `branch -D`.
- A failure prints MOE_WORKTREE_REMOVE_REFUSED and leaves W registered.
- An unregistered directory under .worktrees/ prints MOE_WORKTREE_UNREGISTERED and is never deleted, with at most one #general alert per path per 24h.
- An RPC failure or an unreadable state aborts the pass.
acceptanceCriteria: The QA approval of a fully landed task removes W and its branch; the control .serena/memories and .claude/skills sentinels are byte-identical (both harnesses).
The sweep removes a DONE task's W with an unlanded commit only after refs/moe/rescue/<taskId>/<ts> resolves to that commit (reason worktree-orphan); dirty W bytes are on a rescue ref too.
A WORKING task, an open attempt or W/.moe is never touched; a held sweep.lock skips the pass; at most 5 removals per pass.
An unregistered .worktrees/ directory prints MOE_WORKTREE_UNREGISTERED and stays; a forced unlink failure prints MOE_WORKTREE_REMOVE_REFUSED and leaves W registered.
Existing postflight and worktree-landing cases pass unchanged; the sh/ps1 MOE_(WORKTREE|LAND|CONTROL|BOARD)_ token sets are equal; parity-check passes.
invariants: Nothing is ever deleted through a link, outside W, or without a rescue ref holding every unlanded commit and non-DENY dirty byte.
An RPC failure never counts as unknown to the daemon; TASK_NOT_FOUND is the only unknown signal.
Shared mode (control not on moe/control) runs no new git command and prints no new line.
compatibility: The fake proxy is byte-identical except for get_context view:'status' reads, which no wrapper sent before this task.
No new daemon tool or field; no docs (WT-17/WT-18 own them); grok trusted_folders are untouched.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- (1) Split WT-14 into a removal-engine row plus a sweep row. Rejected:
  - The DoD is human-owned and covers both, so the split would loop back to PLANNING.
  - Each half would still exceed 400 LOC as twins plus harnesses.
  - Every WT row edits the same four files, so a split buys no parallelism. One row plus one measured waiver follows WT-07's precedent.
- (2) Learn 'open attempt' from a default get_context, whose workspace key appears only with an open attempt (WT-02). Rejected: the default read stamps contextFetchedBy on every DONE task it probes, which is board churn. The status view writes nothing, and the wrapper already reads .moe/attempts read-only (moe_attempt_read, moe_seat_finalizing_attempts).
- (3) Use list_tasks for statuses. Rejected: it is paginated (max 500) and cannot tell unknown from paged-out. Per-id status reads give TASK_NOT_FOUND, which is the only unknown signal.
- (4) Unlock, then remove. Changed to a double-force remove with no unlock: if the remove fails, W keeps its lock against a cross-OS prune. The outcome is otherwise identical.
- (5) Rescue inside the QA path. Rejected: §1.7 gives every ambiguous W to the sweep. QA only removes when nothing needs rescuing.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Post-flight:
  - FINAL_STATUS comes from moe_rpc_unserved get_context (moe-agent.sh ~8657-8730).
  - The task-holding branch ends with finalize_postflight (~8940), MOE_LANDING_DONE and live_marker_remove.
  - The loop top has the wrapper reload hash check (~6533), just above `# -------- Pre-flight: perform startup rituals` (~6586).
- moe_rpc writes a JSON-RPC error to stderr and returns 1.
  - launch_outage_release (~6222) parses data.codeName.
  - ps1 Invoke-MoeRpc sets $script:MoeRpcFailure and $script:MoeRpcCodeName.
  - The daemon's missing task is codeName TASK_NOT_FOUND (util/errors.ts notFoundCodeName; getContext.ts throws it before the view switch).
- get_context view 'status' (util/contextStatus.ts) returns task {id, status, ...} and never stamps contextFetchedBy. The default view does stamp it (getContext.ts ~518).
- rescue_ref REASON CAND / rescue_ref_from_commit SHA REASON:
  - they use $MOE_TOP, $LAND_TASK_ID and $FROZEN_TREE as globals;
  - they announce MOE_RESCUE_REF in #general and record_commit kind rescue;
  - rescue_ref returns 1 both for 'nothing to rescue' and for failure.
  - The ps1 twin is Invoke-MoeRescueRef -Git -TaskId -Reason [-Attr|-Sha].
- Temp hook and gate worktrees live in mktemp dirs, never under .worktrees/.
- Attempt closing: moving a task to DONE closes its handed-back attempts, and a finalizing attempt refuses DONE (taskStore.ts assertNoFinalizingAttempt). A DONE row with an open attempt is therefore an edge case, and the re-check still guards it.
- The fake proxy:
  - its get_context has a context-count side effect that flips attempt-postflight to finalizing;
  - it logs chat_send to `<channel>.jsonl` and record_commit to record_commit.jsonl.
planningNotes.risks:
- Junctions: `worktree remove --force` that recursed through a junction would delete the control's .serena/memories and .claude/skills. Unlink-first with verify, the parent-link refusal and the W-itself-a-link refusal are mandatory. Tests check sentinel bytes, not only existence.
- rescue_ref's ambiguous return 1: proceed only on a ref that resolves to the expected commit.
- The sweep runs before the claim, so the fake must answer WORKING for unmapped status reads. Otherwise worktree-mode scenarios that pre-build W with FAKE_TASK_STATUS=DONE would lose W at the loop top.
- WSL/Windows spellings: repair before acting, and use normalized comparisons, never raw ones.
- A lagging local target in remote mode only costs an extra rescue ref, never a loss.
- Root runners ignore chmod: WT14D SKIPs visibly there. CI runs as non-root.
- Size: about 800-1000 net LOC across five files. File the measured waiver at step 5 before the harness runs.
